summary:
The SP category is the story of the season right now — R1 and R2 are both running 63% at n=174 over the last 14 days on starting pitcher ratings, a full 10.3 points above their season baseline, and both carry 4-game winning streaks in that cell. R3 isn't far behind at 60% (+6.3pts). That heat matters today because eight of today's fifteen games are full four-way consensus plays, and several sit right in SP-driven spots: LAD (+1.91/+1.90/+1.13/+1.27) gets Blake Snell at home against a rookie call-up in Jackson Kent, and CLE (+1.77 top mark) throws Logan Allen against Detroit's Keider Montero — both look like SP-signal plays riding the hot cell rather than coincidence. Meanwhile runs is cold across the board (R2 on a 5-game runs losing streak, R1 and R3 both at 3L), so any pick leaning heavily on run-differential logic alone — like the tighter ATL @ PHI number (-0.22 to -0.48, smallest consensus delta on the board) — deserves less confidence today.

On the strong-play side, R4 and R3 are the units to trust: R4 is 27-18 (+8.0u) over 7 days and 54-32 (+19.0u) over 14, while R3 sits at 26-18 (+5.0u) and 50-30 (+20.0u) over the same windows — both clearly outrunning R1 and R2, who are bleeding on the 7-day (R1 -1.0u, R2 -5.0u). That tilts today's close calls toward R3/R4 when the four ratings split, which happens in three games: CHC @ MIA, ARI @ HOU, and MIN @ CHW. In each, R4 is either the lone dissenter or aligns with the smaller-delta consensus, so weight those picks down. Elsewhere, the NYY @ SDP fade (all four models on SDP, deltas -1.3 to -1.9) is the widest gap on the board and lines up with the trends+sp combo, the best-performing category pairing this season at 57.1%. BAL is a name to treat carefully even though it's picked today (+1.05 R1) — BAL's strong-play record is a season-worst 7-10 (-3.0u) among high-volume teams, a red flag against the model's own SDP-style confidence there.
